I've seen the current draft — 12 baseline workers, scale out at 100 jobs in the queue, any available processing region, and a single FIFO queue for all customers. Before I make a binding decision on this, we need to run it through the normal capacity review with FinOps, SRE, security, and customer support. I want to hear any operational requirements or concerns from each of those areas. Who wants to start?

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical for the capacity review. During a separate load investigation this morning, I measured an 11-minute worker startup time during the expected burst pattern. I found that the pipeline needs exactly 6 warm workers with scale-out triggered at exactly 40 queued jobs to keep processing latency within the operating target. I have not yet filed this result in the capacity review. This directly conflicts with the draft's scale-out threshold of 100 queued jobs — at that level, with an 11-minute startup delay, we would blow past our latency targets before any new workers come online.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical security requirement for the capacity review. While checking the image-processing deployment manifest for an unrelated access review, I confirmed that customer-uploaded image data must run in exactly eu-central-1 and use the tenant-managed KMS key named tenant_kms. The current draft permits any available processing region and does not specify that key. This is a hard constraint — if the policy allows workers to spin up in other regions or without that KMS key, we would be processing customer image data outside of its approved boundary. I have not yet opened the security finding on this.
